Verbal Ability -Directions (1-5): Rearrange the five sentences in a logical sequence and then answer the questions given below the paragraph.
 
(A) As the recession deepens, people across the ideological spectrum declare that capitalism has failed.
(B) Yet, recessions are not aberrations of capitalism but an intrinsic part of it.
(C) A bust is an occasion for cleaning out deadwood and failed experiments, and re-inventing capitalism.
(D) Almost every economic news report carries Countries in recession words like ‘crisis’ and ‘disaster’.
(E) Markets create boom and bust cycles, arising from human tendencies to swing from euphoria to fear and back.

questions.questionText:
Fill in the blank with a suitable word from the options.

After centuries of obscurity, this philosopher’s thesis is enjoying a surprising ____ .
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with a suitable word from the options.

After centuries of obscurity, this philosopher’s thesis is enjoying a surprising ____ .
questions.solutionText: Ans - D The sentence tells us that the thesis has been in obscurity (forgotten or neglected) but now it is being revived. We can say it is undergoing a renaissance (revival).
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - D

The sentence tells us that the thesis has been in obscurity (forgotten or neglected) but now it is being revived. We can say it is undergoing a renaissance (revival).

questions.questionText:
Fill in the blank with suitable words from the options.

There is a general ____ in the United States that our ethics are declining and that our moral standards are ____.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with suitable words from the options.

There is a general ____ in the United States that our ethics are declining and that our moral standards are ____.
questions.solutionText: Ans - D The conjunction ‘and’ usually joins things of similar meaning or weight. This suggests that since ethics are declining, moral standards are also declining (deteriorating). Almost any word except ‘optimism’ would have fit the first blank.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - D

The conjunction ‘and’ usually joins things of similar meaning or weight. This suggests that since ethics are declining, moral standards are also declining (deteriorating). Almost any word except ‘optimism’ would have fit the first blank.

options.html: feeling - normalizing
idea - futile
optimism - improving
complaint - deteriorating

questions.questionText:
Fill in the blank with suitable words from the options.


In the Middle Ages, the ____ of the great cathedrals did not enter into the architects’ plans; almost invariably a cathedral was positioned haphazardly in ____ surroundings.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with suitable words from the options.

In the Middle Ages, the ____ of the great cathedrals did not enter into the architects’ plans; almost invariably a cathedral was positioned haphazardly in ____ surroundings.
questions.solutionText: Ans - A The semicolon indicates that the second part of the sentence expands on the first part. So, the second part tells us we are talking about the position, or situation of a cathedral. And since the first part tells us that architects did not pay attention to the situation, the cathedral was positioned randomly in odd (incongruous) surroundings.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - A

The semicolon indicates that the second part of the sentence expands on the first part.

So, the second part tells us we are talking about the position, or situation of a cathedral. And since the first part tells us that architects did not pay attention to the situation, the cathedral was positioned randomly in odd (incongruous) surroundings.

options.html: situation - incongruous
location - apt
ambience - salubrious
durability - convenient

questions.questionText: The quantum theory was initially regarded as absurd, unnatural and ____ with common sense.
questions.questionHtml: The quantum theory was initially regarded as absurd, unnatural and ____ with common sense.
questions.solutionText: Ans - C A set of words linked with ‘and’ usually indicates things of similar weight. To go with ‘absurd’ and ‘unnatural’ we can choose incompatible with common sense.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - C

A set of words linked with ‘and’ usually indicates things of similar weight. To go with ‘absurd’ and ‘unnatural’ we can choose incompatible with common sense.

questions.questionText: Abraham Lincoln was famously known for his ______, which explains why he is often referred to as “Honest Abe.”
questions.questionHtml: Abraham Lincoln was famously known for his ______, which explains why he is often referred to as “Honest Abe.”
questions.solutionText: Ans - C Here, the keyword is “honest,” and the missing word is used to explain why Lincoln was called honest. Thus, the missing word must also mean honesty, as only someone known for honesty would be called “honest.”, As veracity means honesty or truthfulness, it’s the suitable answer.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - C

options.html: mendacity
humility
veracity
piety

questions.questionText:
Fill in the blanks with suitable answer options.


Archaeology is a poor profession; only ____ sums are available for excavating sites and even more ____ amounts for preserving the excavations.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blanks with suitable answer options.

Archaeology is a poor profession; only ____ sums are available for excavating sites and even more ____ amounts for preserving the excavations.
questions.solutionText: Ans - A The part after the semicolon expands upon the first part of the sentence. So, since the first part tells us that there is no money in archaeology, then there will only be small (paltry) amounts for excavating. Also ‘even more’ indicates that another similar word is required. Thus, meager also means small.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - A

The part after the semicolon expands upon the first part of the sentence.

So, since the first part tells us that there is no money in archaeology, then there will only be small (paltry) amounts for excavating. Also ‘even more’ indicates that another similar word is required. Thus, meager also means small.

options.html: paltry - meager
miniscule - substantial
average - augmented
judicious - penurious

questions.questionText: The village headman was unlettered, but he was no fool, he could see through the ________ of the businessman’s proposition and promptly _______ him down.
questions.questionHtml: The village headman was unlettered, but he was no fool, he could see through the ________ of the businessman’s proposition and promptly _______ him down.
questions.solutionText: Ans - D The sentence suggests that although the village headman was illiterate, he was wise. This information must have been provided in order to validate that he could see through the deception (sophistry) of the businessman’s proposition and must have turned him down.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - D

The sentence suggests that although the village headman was illiterate, he was wise. This information must have been provided in order to validate that he could see through the deception (sophistry) of the businessman’s proposition and must have turned him down.

options.html: deception, forced
naivete, turned
potential, forced
sophistry, turned

questions.questionText: Moths are nocturnal pollinators, visiting scented flowers during the hours of darkness, whereas the butterflies are ____ , attracted to bright flowers in the daytime.
questions.questionHtml: Moths are nocturnal pollinators, visiting scented flowers during the hours of darkness, whereas the butterflies are ____ , attracted to bright flowers in the daytime.
questions.solutionText: Ans - A ‘Whereas’ indicates opposite ideas. So we need a word in contrast to ‘nocturnal’ (active at night). The word is diurnal (active in daytime).
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - A

‘Whereas’ indicates opposite ideas. So we need a word in contrast to ‘nocturnal’ (active at night). The word is diurnal (active in daytime).

options.html: ephemeral

questions.questionText: War has been, throughout history, the chief _________ of social cohesion; and since science began, it has been the strongest ________ to technical progress.
questions.questionHtml: War has been, throughout history, the chief _________ of social cohesion; and since science began, it has been the strongest ________ to technical progress.
questions.solutionText: Ans - D In the given space of time i.e. ’throughout history’ there can be only source. Reason and cause or origin can be a particular event. Boost, encouragement and incentive mean the same.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - D

In the given space of time i.e. ’throughout history’ there can be only source. Reason and cause or origin can be a particular event.

Boost, encouragement and incentive mean the same.

options.html: reason, encouragement
origin, boost
cause, provocation
source, incentive

questions.questionText: Scrooge, in the famous novel by Dickens, was a ______; he hated the rest of mankind.
questions.questionHtml: Scrooge, in the famous novel by Dickens, was a ______; he hated the rest of mankind.
questions.solutionText: Ans - A The part of the sentence after the semicolon defines the word needed for the blank. So, since he ‘hated mankind’, the word we need is misanthrope (hater of the rest of mankind).
questions.solutionHtml:

questions.questionText: In a fit of ____ she threw out the valuable statue simply because it had belonged to her ex-husband.
questions.questionHtml: In a fit of ____ she threw out the valuable statue simply because it had belonged to her ex-husband.
questions.solutionText: Ans - A She threw out a valuable statue just because it belonged to her ex-husband. Therefore, she must have been acting out of spite or ill will. Hence we choose pique which means ‘resentment’.

questions.questionText:
Fill in the blanks with the correct answer.

In this biography we are given a glimpse of the young man ______ pursuing the path of the poet despite ______ and rejection slips.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blanks with the correct answer.

In this biography we are given a glimpse of the young man ______ pursuing the path of the poet despite ______ and rejection slips.
questions.solutionText: Ans - A The word ’despite’ indicates something contrary. So, despite the rejection slips he pursues his path doggedly or tirelessly. But since the ‘and’ links similar things he is getting disappointment along with the rejection slips, not encouragement.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans - A

The word ’despite’ indicates something contrary. So, despite the rejection slips he pursues his path doggedly or tirelessly. But since the ‘and’ links similar things he is getting disappointment along with the rejection slips, not encouragement.

options.html: doggedly - disappointment
sporadically - awards
tirelessly - encouragement
successfully - acclaim

questions.questionText:

The assumption that chlorofluorocarbons would be _________ in the environment because they were chemically inert, was challenged by the demonstration of a potential threat to the ozone layer.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with the correct answer.

The assumption that chlorofluorocarbons would be _________ in the environment because they were chemically inert, was challenged by the demonstration of a potential threat to the ozone layer.
questions.solutionText: Ans - B Turn the sentence around, and fit a word of your own in the blank. The demonstration of the potential threat challenged the assumption that the CFCs would be ‘harmless’ because they were inert. Innocuous is the best word because it means harmless.
